testcase.name: every restore failure path clears the previously cached model
the newest model is never auto-activated
two simultaneous deactivations are safe and leave no active model
restore racing with activation and deactivation never leaves disk and cache on different models
an activation referencing a deleted model restores safely inactive
an activation referencing a model that lost replay validation restores safely
a missing, malformed, or unsupported model is rejected safely
a replay-validated model activates and survives service recreation
activate versus deactivate on the same model leaves disk and cache consistent
deactivation removes the active model and its persisted state
restore after the active model's activation file becomes corrupt clears the cache
a corrupt activation file starts safely with no active model
restore after the active model's activation file is deleted clears the cache
a failed activation retains the previous active model
a failed deactivation retains the current model and returns an error
listing models reports replay validation and active state
concurrent activation and deactivation never leaves disk and cache on different models
a missing activation file is a normal inactive state, not corruption
